question.text: What gave US Venture Capital a further boost and enabled bank participation in VC investing?

answer.text: Small Business Investment Act 1958 (recognition, tax breaks, bank participation)

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 21 of the source describes the Small Business Investment Act 1958 as the legislation that recognised small business investment companies, gave them tax breaks, brought them under Small Business Administration regulation, and permitted banks to invest — together giving the US VC industry a major further boost. The Trap: Page 20 of the source notes that US institutional venture funds already existed around the 1940s-50s, so 1958 was a further boost rather than the very first institutionalising moment. The 1929 crash, dotcom bubble and 2008 Great Recession were market events, not VC-enabling legislation. Note: Use the Act's specific features — recognition, tax breaks, SBA oversight, bank participation — when citing why it mattered.
